stories.headline: Karnataka High Court stays GBA's animal waste collection notice
stories.deck: HC stays GBA's animal waste collection notice
stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: The Karnataka High Court on Saturday stayed a public notice issued by the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) on collection and processing of animal waste..The notice covered the scientific collection, transportation and processing of chicken waste, mutton waste, fish waste, other animal waste, and bone waste..Justice B M Shyam Prasad passed the interim order after hearing a petition filed by the Karnataka Poultry Traders Association..The public notice directed imposition of service charges of Rs 5 per kg on animal waste and Rs 3 per kg on animal bone waste. It mandated that the waste has to be handed over to notified private service providers. In addition, the notice prescribed penalties ranging from Rs 2,000 to Rs 3,000 and warned of cancellation of trade licence in case of failure to comply with these regulations..3 months to 30 minutes: GBA introduces online system to cut down building plan approval time.The petitioners contended that GBA’s action is in violation of the Greater Bengaluru Governance Act as well as the fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution..They further contended that the public notice does not consider that some Poultry Meat Centres (PMCs) have a scientific method of treating the waste generated, which includes, depending on the arrangement with the industry involved, packing the waste within a timeframe and handing it over to the representative concerned to be used as raw material by that industry..When there is a contract with pharmaceutical companies that manufacture animal feed, PMCs package the feathers and hand them over to the representatives within eight hours, at a price much higher than what is now stipulated. They said a similar procedure was followed for other waste as well, depending on the industry..After hearing the petition, the court observed that if the GBA did not consider the process explained by the petitioners before publishing the notice, it must give them an opportunity. The court adjourned the hearing to November 5.

stories.headline: Karnataka hikes PUC-2 exam fees by 50%
stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: The examination fees for PUC-2 courses have been increased by 50% and the same will be applicable for the ongoing academic year and March/April 2027 final exams..As per an order issued by the department of school education and literacy, the examination fees will be Rs 600 for fresh and private candidates as against the existing Rs 400..The order says the fees have been revised after almost eight years, with the last revision in 2018. .The fine for paying the fees after the deadline has also been increased..Karnataka govt hikes PUC testing fees citing rise in operational costs.For example, the PUC-2 exam fees with the fine for a ten-day delay will be Rs 750 and the special fine will be Rs 1,980. .The department has also increased the fees for all exam-related services by 50%, including for issuance of marks card, marks card verification, etc..There were no fixed fees for marks card verification, but from now on, the fees for marks card verification for DGCA and for Foreign universities will be Rs 2,000.

stories.headline: Olympiad: Erigaisi picks first win of tournament; India's winning juggernaut rolls on
stories.deck: Arjun Erigaisi bounced back from a difficult start to the Chess Olympiad with a convincing victory over Maksim Chigaev, helping defending champions India beat Spain 3-1 in Round 4. Gukesh continued his impressive run, while Praggnanandhaa and Nihal Sarin drew. India’s women also remained unbeaten, beating Mongolia 3-1 as both Indian teams maintained their winning momentum in Samarkand.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad began on a murky note, with multiple teams facing accommodation issues upon arrival in host city Samarkand, Uzbekistan. India, the defending champions across both the open and women's sections, also had to wait for hours before players were allotted separate rooms. Coming off a gruelling week back home for the Global Chess League (GCL), one of the players who had to hop straight from the Bengaluru event to Samarkand was India's No. 2 Arjun Erigaisi.
When Praggnanandhaa opted to rest for the opening-day fixture against Thailand, it was Arjun who stepped in to play Board 1. Playing white, he lost to Thailand's 2363-rated International Master Prin Laohawirapap.
World champion Gukesh, who has had a commendable score of 3.5/4 in this tournament, explained what had gone wrong for Arjun. "Arjun's first game was very unfortunate, but also worth mentioning that we had very hectic travel and then the first day there were some organisation issues," Gukesh said in an interview with FIDE after his Round 3 win over Italy's Sabino Brunello. "So, Arjun got a room probably a few hours before he went. I mean, we all waited for like six hours to get a room. So obviously, in the first round, Arjun was just tired, and he blundered in the end."
Gukesh added that things had improved since then. "The first day was a bit tricky for all of us, but after that, I think we are all rested. We are all looking forward to the games and all good," he said.
Those words showed up in the results on Saturday, when Arjun took down Maksim Chigaev to secure his first win of the tournament, helping India beat Spain 3-1.
How Arjun Erigaisi won his first game at the 2026 Chess Olympiad
Arjun Erigaisi, playing white, produced a controlled attacking performance against Maksim Chigaev.
The opening was a flexible Réti/English setup, with White gaining space through 12.h4 and 13.h5, provoking ...g5 and creating long-term kingside targets.
After 14.d5, White secured a useful space advantage while Black’s pieces became somewhat passive.
The key strategic phase began with 17.Nh2 and 18.Bh3, followed by the exchange of bishops on c8. Erigaisi then expanded with 21.e4 and 23.f4, correctly opening lines while Black’s king remained vulnerable.
The sequence 28.Qe4 Rxf1 29.Rxf1 Rf8 30.Rxf8+ simplified the rooks and left White with a dangerous queen-and-knight attack.
The decisive phase was 31.Qh7, followed by 32.Qh8+ and 33.Ng4, coordinating queen and knight around the exposed king. After 34.Nxe5+, Black could not escape the perpetual-looking checks, and 36.Qf7+ ended the game.
Elsewhere on the board, Gukesh continued his fine run, beating Spain's Alexei Shirov to move to 4.5/5 and continuing a solid turnaround from Thursday's dip below the 2700 rating mark.
Praggnanandhaa and Nihal Sarin both drew their games, enough for India to close out the tie 3-1.
For Erigaisi specifically, the win carries added significance. As India's second-highest rated player and a regular on Board 1 or 2 duty, a winless start would have added pressure to an already long season that had him travelling directly from the GCL in Bengaluru to Samarkand with barely any time to recover. Saturday's result suggests that adjustment period may now be behind him.
India's winning juggernaut marches on
India's women's team also kept their unbeaten run alive, beating Mongolia 3-1. Koneru Humpy and Vaishali Rameshbabu both drew their games against lower-rated opposition.
But Divya Deshmukh and Savitha Shri won on the lower boards to see the team through comfortably, continuing a campaign that has yet to drop a match tie.
With both squads now through four rounds without a defeat as a team, the tests only get tougher from here. India will take on Poland in the women's section on Sunday, while the open team faces a mouthwatering clash against Anish Giri's Dutch side, arguably the sternest test either Indian team has faced so far in Samarkand.

stories.headline: Samrat Choudhary promises jobs to one crore women
stories.deck: Addressing the gathering, Samrat Choudhary said that women in Bihar are moving forward rapidly, and their growing economic, social, and political participation reflects the State’s changing landscape
stories.bodyText:
BiharChief MinisterSamrat Choudhary on Saturday (September 19, 2026) announced plans to link 1 crore women with employment opportunities. He also said that the government will provide fellowships to 1,000 women to pursue a PhD, and under this fellowship, a monthly stipend of ₹10,000 will be provided for four years. He announced this during the 25th foundation day of the Bihar State Women Commission.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Choudhary said that women in Bihar are moving forward rapidly, and their growing economic, social and political participation reflects the State’s changing landscape.
He added that the provision of 50% reservation for women in Panchayati Raj institutions and urban local bodies has significantly strengthened their participation. He also noted that ‘Jeevika’ has played an important role in making women economically strong.
“The government aims to directly link 1 crore women to employment opportunities. Under the school uniform scheme, arrangements are being made to provide uniforms prepared by ‘Jivika Didis’ [women from self-help groups] instead of distributing cash to students; this initiative will also create new employment avenues,” Mr. Choudhary said.
He mentioned that incentive schemes are currently operational in Bihar to promote the education of female students at the matriculation, intermediate, and undergraduate levels, and assistance is also being provided to students preparing for competitive examinations.
“Through the Girls’ PhD Fellowship, a target has been set to provide financial aid of ₹10,000 per month to 1,000 female students annually for higher education and research. Efforts are underway to establish a university dedicated to women to further expand opportunities for women’s higher education,”Mr. Choudhary said.
Speaking on women’s safety, the Chief Minister pointed out that the introduction of the ‘Police Didi’ system in the State is a step ahead on this front, adding that female police personnel are being deployed near schools, colleges and other educational institutions to ensure the safety of girl students calling it a pioneering initiative by Bihar.
He urged the Commission not to limit itself merely to resolving complaints but also to offer regular suggestions to the government for improving the status of women.
“I want the Women’s Commission to become a factory for creating political activists. The Commission should play an active role in empowering women socially, economically, and politically,”Mr. Choudhary said.
In the presence of the Commission’s Chairperson, Apsara Mishra, the Bihar CM said that women’s empowerment forms a crucial foundation for Bihar’s prosperity and expressed confidence that the Commission would continue to work tirelessly leading up to its golden jubilee — to integrate women into the mainstream of development and safeguard their rights and dignity.
A short film based on the Commission’s 25-year journey was screened during the event, and to mark the Silver Jubilee, the Chief Minister released a special postage stamp dedicated to the Commission—in collaboration with the Department of Posts—and unveiled the Commission’s souvenir.
Published - September 20, 2026 03:20 am IST

stories.headline: U.S. military says it killed 4 in strike on alleged drug-smuggling boat in Caribbean
stories.deck: As with most of the military's statements on strikes in the eastern Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea, U.S. Southern Command said it targeted the alleged drug traffickers along known smuggling routes.
stories.bodyText:
The U.S. military attacked a boat suspected of being used to smuggle drugs in the Caribbean Sea, killing four people, as the Trump administration continues its months-long campaign against alleged traffickers in Latin America.
The attack on Saturday (September 19, 2026) brings the number of people who have been killed in boat strikes by the U.S. military to at least 231 in 69 strikes since the Trump administration began targeting those it calls “narcoterrorists” almost a year ago.
As with most of the military's statements on strikes in the eastern Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea, U.S. Southern Command said it targeted the alleged drug traffickers along known smuggling routes.
The military did not provide evidence that the vessel was ferrying drugs. A video posted on X showed an image of what appeared to be a moving boat followed by a flash.
Also Read | U.S. military launches new airstrikes to ‘swiftly punish’ Iran for deaths of U.S. troops
The Trump administration is pursuing deals with allied nations to extend its offensive to land across multiple Latin American countries.
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said during a visit to Panama last month that Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras had agreed to allow the U.S. to carry out joint military operations against criminal groups on their soil.
Guatemala denied reaching such a deal. Ecuador launched similar missions with the US in March.
President Donald Trump has said the U.S. is in “armed conflict” with cartels in Latin America and has justified the attacks as a necessary escalation to stem the flow of drugs into the United States and fatal overdoses claiming American lives.
But his administration has offered little evidence to support its claims of killing smugglers. (AP)

briefs.headline: 1,200 girls to get AI coaching across 17 govt degree colleges
briefs.deck: AI coaching for girls in govt degree colleges
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: In a bid to improve the employment prospects of girl students pursuing non-technical courses at state-run degree colleges, the Karnataka government is rolling out a dedicated programme wherein they will be offered training in Artificial Intelligence (AI)..The ‘Women and AI’ initiative will be rolled out at 17 colleges where students pursuing commerce and arts courses will be provided the opportunity to add AI to their skillset..As part of the programme, students will learn the fundamentals of AI, use of AI for data analysis, use of tools such as ChatGPT, using AI to build resumes, ethics of AI, among other topics. As many as 1,253 girls from the 17 government colleges selected for the initiative in the first phase..The Higher Education Department is implementing the programme in collaboration with Learning Links Foundation. “The initiative will enable students to familiarise themselves with AI. The programme, wherein technical experts will be enlisted to teach the students about AI, will be rolled out soon,” said an official from the Higher Education Department..Rising warnings over AI risks are colliding with strategic competition.Higher Education Minister Basavaraj Rayareddi said that the programme was aimed at helping girl students achieve independence by equipping them with technical skills and knowledge about AI. “This will definitely help them secure jobs,” he said..The programme will be spread out across 20-30 hours. The Higher Education Department is also planning to launch a programme called ‘Mentor Together’ wherein 35,000 students from 198 government degree colleges will be imparted training in key skills. Job melas will also be organised as part of the initiative.

briefs.headline: ‘Nobody gives a chance, one must grab it’: Siddaramaiah on Sindhia
briefs.deck: Siddu: None gives chance, one must grab it
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: “He became a minister before me! Later, I became the chief minister twice, but Sindhia hasn’t,” former CM Siddaramaiah said on Saturday, drawing laughter from the audience at the launch of the biography of veteran Congress leader P G R Sindhia..“What? Give him a chance? Nobody gives a chance. One has to grab the chance! One must work in a way that earns it. But Sindhia had all qualifications to become chief minister,” Siddaramaiah said..On the occasion, he released the book ‘A Life Uncompromised: The Dr P G R Sindhia Story’, authored by retired IAS officer K K Khandelwal to mark Sindhia’s 78th birthday and 45 years in public life..The former chief minister traced their shared political journey from Ramakrishna Hegde and H D Deve Gowda cabinets, recalling how Sindhia handled youth, home, transport, social welfare and finance portfolios with “discipline and efficiency”. He said the title ‘Uncompromised’ fits Sindhia’s style..“When he became finance minister, he told me, ‘I have instructions to look for whatever mistakes you might have made’,” he recounted, referring to his own long stint as finance minister under multiple chief ministers..Low-key housewarming ceremony of former CM Siddaramaiah in Mysuru.Highlighting Sindhia’s organisational strengths, Siddaramaiah said he worked “very fast” during Council, Rajya Sabha and Assembly elections, managing people and tasks without complaining..He also credited Sindhia’s wife, Geetha, for holding the family together and enabling his public service..Khandelwal spoke about how the book idea took shape, recounting Sindhia’s rise from humble beginnings in Doddamaralavadi village to senior ministerial and party roles..Suttur seer Shivarathri Deshikendra Swami was among the chief guests. Ministers U T Khader, Eshwar Khandre and Basavaraj Rayareddi were present on the occasion.

briefs.headline: Rajagopal Reddy’s truce with Revanth: What changed in Telangana Congress?
briefs.deck: Revanth's growing clout in Telangana is new Cong dilemma
briefs.bodyText: Hyderabad: In August, Congress leader and Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajagopal Reddy targeted his own government during a public event in Hyderabad with veiled remarks about "outsiders" holding key positions. Many saw it as an indirect jibe at Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy..Rajagopal Reddy, younger brother of Cabinet minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy, has made no secret of his political ambitions and desire for recognition of his regional leadership — a stance that previously strained his relations with the CM’s camp..He never minced words and, on one occasion, even alleged that leaders who recently joined the party were seeking to capture it and wield disproportionate power, warning that he would not remain a silent spectator..Long seen as a rebel within the party, Rajagopal Reddy briefly quit the Congress for the BJP before returning in the days leading up to the 2023 Telangana Assembly elections. His brother and fellow MLA, Venkat Reddy, currently serves as the state's roads and buildings minister..Rajagopal Reddy's discontent is widely believed to stem from being denied a berth in the Telangana Cabinet, and he rarely misses a chance to criticise Revanth Reddy, something that appears to have quietly impressed many within the Congress rank and file..That changed on September 5. Rajagopal Reddy, who skipped several of the CM’s meetings in his home district of erstwhile Nalgonda, showed up with a large entourage at a public meeting in Nakrekal, where Revanth Reddy was present..The two leaders embraced warmly, publicly setting aside months of political friction and speculation of a rift within the Telangana Congress over governance and key appointments. Rajagopal Reddy later went further, dismissing talk of a rift altogether and emphasising cooperation within the state leadership, a marked shift from a leader who had until then tested the limits of the party's tolerance for internal dissent..This came just two days after senior leader Konda Surekha was removed from the Cabinet. The move, which the All India Congress Committee (AICC) was believed to have backed, signalled to the party's rank and file just how far Revanth Reddy's influence within the central leadership extended..The effect.Rajagopal Reddy's swift capitulation soon after suggested that years of resistance to the CM might have finally given way to accommodation. It also laid bare the balancing act facing the Congress high command in Telangana, which is now caught between the party's old guard and its newer entrants..Telangana CM Revanth Reddy thanks Centre for houses under PMAY-G, seeks more for state.This tension — between the "old Congress" and a party now substantially reshaped by Revanth Reddy — has only sharpened since Surekha's exit. Notably, Revanth will complete a decade in the Congress next year; in that span, he has risen from PCC chief to CM, a post he has now held for close to three years, and is credited with steering the party to power in Telangana for the first time since the state's formation a decade earlier..For now, the AICC appears firmly aligned with Revanth's agenda, largely setting aside old-timers’ grievances. Party veteran T Jeevan Reddy — a six-time MLA and former minister — was sidelined and eventually crossed over to the BRS. Four-time MLA and former minister G Chinna Reddy — another vocal critic of Revanth's leadership — has similarly been left out in the cold..Meanwhile, senior figures such as Deputy CM Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, Industries Minister D Sridhar Babu, and Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy have kept a low profile, appearing resigned to a comparatively junior leader calling the shots. How long this equilibrium holds remains uncertain, with elections still 2.5 years away..Even during the 10-day Surekha episode, these senior leaders maintained a conspicuous silence. Similar undercurrents of tension had surfaced occasionally before the 2023 elections, but relations have been notably smoother since the party's ascent to power, with ministers largely staying out of each other's portfolios..The influence."The Surekha episode is, without doubt, the AICC leadership’s open endorsement of Revanth Reddy's leadership in the state," senior journalist and political analyst Telakapalli Ravi told DH.."If you observe, Revanth has increased his aggression both within the party and outside it after the Surekha episode, as is clearly evident from how he took on ex-CM K Chandrashekar Rao in the Assembly recently, and in sending revenue teams to his farmhouse in Erravelli.”.Reflecting on the broader tensions, Ravi added that this dilemma was not limited to the Congress. "Be it the TDP, the BJP, or any other party, seniors and super-seniors are being sidelined. Party leaderships are encouraging talent purely on merit, capability, and capacity, and are leaning towards the relatively young, even if they come from outside," he said..Another political analyst, who spoke on condition of anonymity, suggested that Surekha may have been a soft target, chosen to help Revanth consolidate his hold on the party and send a stern message to his detractors — one that would have played out very differently had it involved heavyweights such as Uttam Kumar Reddy, Vikramarka, or Sridhar Babu.

US military says it struck suspected drug-trafficking vessel, 4 killed
briefs.bodyText:
The US military said it killed four people in a strike on a vessel in the Caribbean on Saturday, alleging that it was involved in drug trafficking.
“On September 19, under the direction of Southern Command, Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere executed a lethal, kinetic strike on a go-fast vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Caribbean.,” US Southern Command said in a post on X.
"Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel's active involvement in narco-trafficking. The operation killed four narco-terrorists," it added.
The strike is part of a campaign launched last year against what the Trump administration describes as “narco-terrorists”. Rights groups have criticised the operations as “extrajudicial killings”.
The latest strike brings the reported death toll from US military attacks on boats in the eastern Pacific and Caribbean to at least 231 people across 69 strikes since the Trump administration began targeting groups it labels “narcoterrorists” nearly a year ago.
The Trump administration has also sought to expand the campaign on land through cooperation with governments in Latin America. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras had agreed to joint US operations against criminal groups, though Guatemala later denied reaching such an agreement. Ecuador has conducted similar operations with US support since March.
Trump has described the US as being in an “armed conflict” with Latin American cartels and defended the strikes as necessary to curb drug trafficking into the United States and the resulting overdose deaths. The administration, however, has faced criticism over the limited evidence it has publicly provided to substantiate its claims about those killed in the operations.

stories.headline: Monsoon bids goodbye, still Bengaluru may get rain this week
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Just as the southwest monsoon begins its official retreat from parts of the country, Bengaluru could be in for another spell of rain. A weather system developing over the Bay of Bengal is expected to strengthen over the coming days, potentially bringing moderate to heavy isolated thundershowers and much-needed relief from heat.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), a low-pressure area is likely to form over the north Andaman Sea and adjoining areas late Saturday evening. The system is expected to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a depression over the east-central Bay of Bengal on Monday and further into a deep depression over the west-central Bay of Bengal Tuesday. It is then expected to continue moving west-northwestwards towards the west-central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal, reaching near the south Odisha-north Andhra Pradesh coasts by Wednesday.
The fast-developing low-pressure condition over Bay of Bengal system could bring a welcome break from the heat, with the strengthening system expected to draw considerable moisture inland towards the state. The IMD has already issued a yellow alert for coastal districts, Belagavi, Gadag, Dharwad, Haveri, Bidar, Kalaburagi, Chikkamagaluru, Hassan and Kodagu.
Rainfall activity is expected to increase across parts of 
Karnataka
 between Tuesday and Thursday. A senior scientist at IMD, Bengaluru, said: “During this time, there will be a possibility of trough from Marathwada to Southeast Arabian Sea across Interior Karnataka and Keralam resulting in thundershowers in the first half of ensuing week. In South Interior Karnataka districts, the thundershowers are likely to be accompanied by strong, gusty winds measuring 30 to 40 km/hr.”

stories.headline: Bengaluru PG inmates’ complaints prompt police visit
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Around 30 residents of a paying guest (PG) accommodation in Koramangala approached Viveknagar police Saturday, alleging poor living conditions, frequent power disruptions and inadequate maintenance at the facility.
The residents of the Hyphen Sprout PG in Cauvery Colony alleged that they had been facing frequent electricity interruptions, unreliable WiFi, elevator breakdowns and severe cockroach infestation. They also raised concerns over the maintenance and hygiene of the drinking-water and water-tank facilities.
Following a call from the residents, Vivek Nagar police visited the PG and spoke to them. Police officials asked the residents to lodge a formal complaint if they wanted action to be initiated.
Residents said the unreliable internet connection had particularly affected those working remotely and dependent on stable connectivity. “Despite repeated complaints and communications, the property management has frequently failed to provide proper responses or timely resolutions. Residents are often unable to obtain effective assistance from the property managers for basic and essential services,” said Kumar Mayank, a resident.
He also alleged that the drinking-water and water-tank facilities were not cleaned or maintained regularly. Residents claimed they had spotted insects and other crawling organisms inside the water tank, raising concerns over the hygiene and safety of the water supplied to them.
The residents said they had repeatedly brought the issues to the attention of the property management but alleged that their complaints had not been adequately addressed. The PG management is yet to react on the issue.

stories.headline: Varthur-Sarjapur road joins ORR as one of Bengaluru’s most congested stretches
stories.bodyText:
For a commuter driving the nine-km stretch of State Highway-35 between Varthur Kodi and Sarjapur-Ambalipura Road, the journey is an exercise in navigating one hurdle after another. Open drains run alongside the road, mounds of soil occupy non-existent footpaths, thick clouds of dust induce bouts of coughing, and commuters are forced to constantly manoeuvre around potholes along this busy stretch of east Bengaluru.
While the recent incident of schoolchildren struggling in buses for hours exposed the everyday ordeal of commuters in the locality amid crumbling road infrastructure, a recent Bengaluru Traffic Police analysis of congestion has revealed that this State Highway is now among the city’s most congested stretches.
A senior traffic police officer confirmed to The Hindu that this stretch (between Varthur Kodi and Sarjapur Road) has joined the 17.1-km Outer Ring Road (ORR) stretch between Silk Board junction and K.R. Puram Metro as one of the most congested roads in the city. What’s more? On several days, the congestion on SH-35 has surpassed that on the ORR, according to the officer.
“When the congestion data is compiled, it is not just the main corridor whose traffic volume is considered. Even the connecting roads are counted to draw the final congestion length,” the officer explained. “As even the smaller roads are clogged at all points in a day and movement is slowed down, the travel time in the area has shot up multifold. This has led to large volumes on other roads,” he explained.
Explaining why it is overtaking the ORR, the officer said that the ORR stretch witnesses traffic during peak hours, while on weekends it is non-existent. Unlike the ORR, traffic is persistent on SH-35 throughout the day, which makes it notorious.
Limited infrastructure
The locality, which falls under the Mahadevapura Assembly constituency, hosts scores of apartment complexes and more than 20 top schools, making it a busy residential area that also has a mix of tech companies coming up.
Narendra Rao, resident of Gunjur village, puts it like this: “While there are skyscraping apartment complexes, with thousands of vehicles owned by those apartment dwellers, the road infrastructure is very limited. Roads that exist are extremely narrow and incapable of holding the growing vehicle numbers.”
The entire nine-km stretch, barring a few kilometres closer to Sarjapur Road, is dotted with large craters, and at some junctions, such as the Rama Temple near Gunjur Bus Stop, there are no signs of a road.
Three choke points
The nine-km stretch predominantly has three choke points: the junction at Varthur Police Station, the Gunjur-Mugulur Road junction, and the point near the Muthasandra Main Road cross near Varthur Lake. At all these junctions, there are no traffic signals, and vehicle flow is manually managed by traffic police officers and local residents throughout the day.
Prasanna Bhat, Varthur resident who works as a traffic volunteer, explained that the highway is a crucial connecting link in the eastern outskirts and that all heavy vehicles use the stretch. This, coupled with hundreds of school buses and local vehicles, makes the stretch a high-density road.
“With civic works ongoing and bad road conditions, vehicle movement is slow, which naturally creates congestion,” he said. However, what makes it worse is that the slow-moving traffic on this stretch has a ripple effect on the connecting stretches.
Clogged connecting roads
There are over eight major connecting routes to the State Highway, which converge a high volume of vehicles onto the highway. These key connecting stretches include Hosahalli Road, Balagere Main Road, Gunjur-Mugalur Road, Gunjur-Doddakannelli Road, and Gunjur-Balagere Road.
Most of these stretches are narrower, with some even spanning 20 to 25 feet when travelling into the interiors. In addition, these are the roads that bear the maximum load, as the majority of the apartment complexes are located along these stretches.
Naturally, when the State Highway chokes at key junctions, these smaller roads, bearing large volumes of vehicles, see elongated congestion, which extends beyond 1.5 km many times, especially during peak hours.
Footpaths and drains
While motorists bear the brunt of the traffic, residents are left in misery with limited to no pedestrian infrastructure along the stretch, especially near Varthur Police Station.
Rohan, a pedestrian, narrated his ordeal and said: “Crossing the road from one end to another takes five minutes, and walking along the stretch is impossible because the footpaths are either dumped with mounds of mud or the drains are not covered by slabs.”
Adding to the issues is a substantial amount of dust hovering in the air as civic works are ongoing. In many places, pedestrians have to climb up mounds of mud and then climb down to walk along the stretch.
In addition, civic negligence is substantial, with cables lying around, uncovered drains, unmoved construction material, and dumped construction debris.
However, this condition has existed for more than a year, with the Karnataka Road Development Corporation (KRDCL) delaying two civic works: a flyover at Varthur Kodi and the widening of SH-35.
While the project was taken up in 2019, there has been limited on-ground implementation. The original deadline to complete the project was 2021. However, according to GBA sources, the on-ground works are yet to gather pace.
Meanwhile, speaking to The Hindu, Lokhande Snehal Sudhakar, Additional Commissioner, East City Corporation, said: “There was a land acquisition issue, but now we are issuing TDRs to property owners. stories.headline: BMTC inspects seven-metre buses as it plans 200 midi buses despite past record, revenue concerns
stories.deck: The move comes at a time when the corporation has historically faced both safety concerns involving midi buses and financial challenges associated with operating smaller buses.
stories.bodyText:
The Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) has begun inspecting and evaluating different bus models as it explores the induction of 200 seven-metre midi/mini-buses to improve connectivity on narrow roads and in interior parts of the city.
The move comes at a time when the corporation has historically faced both safety concerns involving midi buses and financial challenges associated with operating smaller buses. BMTC is now examining suitable models as the demand for smaller vehicles grows, particularly for first- and last-mile connectivity to Namma Metro stations.
The latest exercise also follows Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh’s recent direction to deploy 200 mini-air-conditioned electric buses within a 5-km radius of Metro stations. The buses are intended to connect residential layouts and neighbourhoods that are difficult to serve with larger buses. The 200 mini-AC buses are part of the 4,500 electric buses being provided to BMTC under the Centre’s PM E-DRIVE scheme.
According to sources, BMTC is now looking at suitable smaller bus models for these operations, with the focus on vehicles that can negotiate narrow roads while providing feeder connectivity.
Previous fire incidents raised safety concerns
BMTC’s experience with midi buses has not been without problems. In January and February 2022, two BMTC buses caught fire within a span of about 10 days, prompting the corporation to seek a safety assessment of its midi-bus fleet.
BMTC had procured 186 midi buses in 2014. The buses were around nine metres long and had about 33 seats, making them smaller than the standard 12-metre buses and suitable for narrower and more congested roads.
An initial investigation into the fires found that the incidents originated in the engine area. A later assessment reported that loose parts in the starter had resulted in a short circuit. BMTC subsequently subjected the buses to detailed inspections before allowing them to return to service.
The safety concerns were among the factors that made BMTC cautious about expanding its smaller-bus fleet.
Revenue economics another hurdle
However, technical and safety issues are not the only challenge. According to officials, the economics of operating mini and midi buses have also made BMTC cautious about expanding their use.
“BMTC assesses bus operations by comparing the cost per kilometre (CPKM) with the earnings per kilometre (EPKM). Smaller buses have lower passenger-carrying capacity but require largely the same basic crew arrangement as bigger buses. A standard 12-metre BMTC bus can carry substantially more passengers than a mini or midi bus, while the driver and conductor costs remain broadly similar. As a result, smaller buses can struggle to generate enough revenue to cover their operating costs, particularly on routes with weak ridership,” an official said.
The issue becomes more significant under the Gross Cost Contract (GCC) model used for several of BMTC’s electric buses. Under this arrangement, a private operator owns and maintains the vehicle while BMTC pays an agreed rate for operating the bus on a per-kilometre basis.
This means BMTC has to pay the contracted amount irrespective of whether a bus is carrying a full load or only a handful of passengers. For feeder services, where passenger demand can vary considerably between peak and non-peak hours, this can increase the corporation’s financial burden.
“Despite these concerns, the expansion of Namma Metro has increased the need for reliable feeder services. With Metro stations extending to more parts of Bengaluru, we expect to play a larger role in connecting neighbourhoods to the Metro network,” an official added.

briefs.headline: Man who killed wife found hanging from a tree in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
A 25-year-old private company employee, who allegedly strangled his wife to death inside a hotel room in Doddaballapur town on September 15, was found hanging from a tree near a lake in his hometown of Gauribidanur.
The deceased, G. Anand, had allegedly escaped from the hotel room after murdering his wife, 
Vidya
, 23. The couple had been married for four years and had a two-and-a-half-year-old son, who is currently staying with Vidya’s parents in Gauribidanur.
Anand’s decomposed body was spotted by passersby, who alerted the police. Police recovered the mobile phones of both Anand and Vidya from his trouser pockets, along with an empty alcohol bottle.
According to family sources, the couple frequently quarrelled over domestic issues. “Vidya had distanced herself from Anand. However, he took her to a hotel room after promising that he would never fight with her again,” police said. He allegedly strangled her to death there.
Helmet godown, mobile shop gutted in accidental fire
Materials stored in a helmet godown and an adjoining mobile phone shop were gutted in an accidental fire at Sudhamanagar in Wilson Garden late Friday night.
Two fire tenders were deployed to the spot and brought the blaze under control within an hour. No casualties were reported, police said.
A preliminary investigation by the police revealed that a short circuit inside the helmet godown may have triggered the fire.

briefs.headline: Tulu steps into the spotlight
briefs.deck: The Karnataka Cabinet has accorded Tulu the status of the state's secondadditional official language in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi
briefs.bodyText:
For a language that has been spoken along 
Karnataka
’s coast for centuries, Tulu’s latest milestone marks a significant new chapter. The Karnataka Cabinet has accorded Tulu the status of the state’s second additional official language in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi, fulfilling a long-standing demand for greater recognition of the language. For actors and filmmakers with roots in Tulunadu, however, Tulu represents more than official recognition.
A recognition of coastal culture
The recognition of Tulu is a moment of pride not just for the language, but for the entire coastal region. Tulu art and culture have powerfully contributed to putting the coastal region on the map. The coastal region's contribution comes through traditions such as Kambala and Yakshagana, as well as fishing and cinema – Shine Shetty
A language rich in culture
I learnt Tulu during my college days as an RJ in Mangaluru, and the more I learnt, the more I discovered its richness in literature and culture. This recognition acknowledges not just the language, but the rich legacy that comes with it. Tulu’s influence extends beyond the coast, with its deep roots in Karnataka’s history – Manvita Kamath
A bigger stage for Tulu cinema
As an actor and Tulu speaker, I believe cinema can take the language to a wider audience. Giving Tulu films the same importance as those in other languages is key to helping both the language and its cinema grow – Roopesh Shetty
Tulunadu at the heart of his storytelling
I was born in Puttur and Tulu is my mother tongue. The culture of Tulunadu has deeply influenced me and found its way into my filmmaking — from the lush, green worlds I create to the characters inspired by people I’ve known – Anup Bhandari
A language that belongs to everyone
Among the many Dravidian languages, Tulu has survived without diluting itself and retained a strong identity. Its beauty lies in the fact that it transcends caste, religion and class, finding a place in every aspect of life, from cinema to everyday conversations. This recognition is a fitting acknowledgement of its importance – Dheekshith Shetty

briefs.headline: World Cleanup Day: Citizens lead plogging drive across Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: It was a clean-up and plogging special for #IamBengaluru – Volunteer for Parks on Saturday, as volunteers across the city marked World Cleanup Day weekend by stepping out to care for Bengaluru’s shared green spaces. The initiative was presented by Multigen and in association with Kristu Jayanti University.
Jakkur lake saw one of the biggest turnouts, with more than 150 volunteers, including students of Gopalan Engineering College, joining the clean-up activity organised by communiTREE and Jalaposhan Trust.
At Girinagar Park, Youth for Seva led the day’s activities, where students of NPS Rajajinagar, under their Project Evara initiative, also demonstrated a textile waste management session. Hasiru Dala led a plogging activity at Nagapura Park, while communiTREE and Smart Soc Hope Foundation brought volunteers together for clean-up and plogging at Lalbagh.
For Hafiz RK, founder & CEO, communiTREE, volunteering is about building a relationship between citizens and shared spaces. “Parks need more than infrastructure. They need people who care for them, spend time in them and take responsibility for them. 
We hope to create not just volunteers for parks, but a community connected to the spaces it shares,” he said.
Nithyanandan, project manager, Hasiru Dala, said, “It is encouraging to see citizens coming together and taking responsibility. When citizens, NGOs and volunteers join hands, we can create greater awareness and make a real difference.”
Valeswara Rao, Volunteer, Jalaposhan Trust, said, “I have been volunteering at Jakkur Lake for the past two years, and I have seen the amount of plastic and dry waste come down drastically. The lake is an important lung space for Bengaluru, and regular volunteering can make a real difference. I urge more Bengalureans to come and join us.”
Dhanush G, Student, Gopalan College of Engineering and Management, added: “We often focus on improving ourselves, but we should also make time to improve our surroundings. If each of us can set aside even one hour a week to care for our lakes, parks and environment, we can leave behind a better city for future generations.”
Adithya, degree student, said, “Having grown up in Bengaluru, I see parks as an essential part of city life and a welcome relief from the concrete around us. Planting and protecting greenery becomes even more important as the city develops. I enjoyed volunteering with my friends and doing our bit for one of Bengaluru’s parks.”
Aadhya, Class 10 Student, NPS Rajajinagar said planting more trees and protecting greenery is important at a time when deforestation is a concern.
Raja Thamizharasan, volunteer, Smart SoC Hope Foundation, said, “Giving one or two hours to a community activity is not a lot of time, but it can make a difference. Instead of spending that time in my room watching reels, I could be outdoors, help clean the environment and do something for nature. It also gives me exercise and a sense of peace, so volunteering is good for both the environment and for me.”
To participate in #IamBengaluru activities, visit https://iambengaluru.co.in

briefs.headline: Boy’s murder: Bengaluru police dig deeper as motive remains a mystery
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Investigations into the kidnap and murder of 13-year-old 
Prajwal
 by his UK-returned neighbour Bhaskar Reddy have turned out to be a major challenge for the cops with regard to establishing the motive behind the murder.
Preliminary investigations pointed to the usual angle: Bhaskar’s family having been trapped in over Rs 3 crore of debt and the evil plan of raising funds by kidnapping a known and vulnerable person for a huge ransom! “But there seems to be more than what meets the eye,” a senior police officer said and added that they were probing from two other angles along with that of ransom demand.
The sequence of events that transpired is one of the reasons for police to explore other angles: Wednesday night, 26-year-old Bhaskar lured Prajwal, son of realtor 
Manohar
, into his car on the pretext of buying crackers and teaching him to drive. His associate Edukondalu was also in the car. After taking the boy to a land parcel in Bagalur that his father planned to buy, they allegedly gagged him, tied his hands and legs with plastic wire and recorded a video of him crying. Bhaskar had planned to send the video to Manohar, threatening that Prajwal would be harmed unless Rs 1.5 crore was paid. But before sending the video, the duo killed Prajwal and Bhaskar was driving towards Nellore in Andhra Pradesh to dispose of the body when he got caught after getting involved in a road accident.
A senior police officer said: “He was telling us that he knew the boy’s father had cash as the latter planned to buy some land and decided to kidnap the boy for ransom. But the questions unanswered are: Why didn’t he make the ransom call to the father? Why did he consume alcohol when he planned to drive outside Bengaluru to dispose of the body? Why didn’t he think he would get caught when he was last seen in public with Prajwal? We are not completely believing Bhaskar’s theory; we are probing from multiple angles.”
Police said they are also probing if any differences had cropped up, financially and friendship-wise, between Manohar’s family and Bhaskar’s family. While Bhaskar’s family was in debt, Manohar was thriving, cops said. This apart, the cops are checking if Bhaskar had developed animosity towards Prajwal in recent times. A cop said: “We have learnt that Prajwal had become very close to Bhaskar and had started teasing him over his romantic interest. This did not go well with Bhaskar. We have seized Bhaskar’s mobile phone and are analyzing all communications in the run up to the crime and before his arrest.” The police are yet to trace Bhaskar’s associate Edukondalu, who was present during the killing, to know more about the motive.
From London to lockup
Family sources told cops that after completing PU (Science) in Nellore, Bhaskar completed his BTech at Reva University in Bengaluru between 2017 and 2021. Then, he flew to London to pursue an MSc in Construction Management. The 18-month course began in Jan 2022. After completing the course, Bhaskar did various part-time jobs before flying back to Bengaluru in Jan 2025. Since then, he has worked in different private companies for shorter periods. For the last one and a half months, he has been working with L&T Finance Ltd in the Koramangala branch. He earned Rs 65,000 per month. But this income was meagre for him as Bhaskar’s lifestyle included alcohol, SUVs, friends and parties, police said.

briefs.headline: Karnataka eyes Rs 15k crore chip investment, 2k jobs
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: 
Karnataka
 could attract over Rs 15,000 crore in investment and more than 2,000 jobs after talks with over 20 companies at Semicon India 2026 in New Delhi, industries minister MB Patil, who is attending the event, said Saturday. briefs.headline: Karnataka Lokayukta orders probe into poor-quality school shoes
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Lokayukta has ordered a preliminary investigation into allegations that poor-quality shoes supplied to govt schoolchildren in 16 districts were getting damaged within days, with stitching reportedly coming apart within minutes of use.
Upalokayukta Justice B Veerappa took suo motu cognisance of media reports about the alleged poor quality of the footwear. Complaints have been registered against the concerned deputy directors of the school education department and block education officers in the districts under the jurisdiction of Upalokayukta-2. The districts include Ballari, Bagalkote, Bengaluru Rural, Bidar, Haveri, Belagavi, Mandya, Dakshina Kannada, Davanagere, Kalaburagi, Tumakuru, Udupi, Vijayanagar, Raichur, Koppal and Kolar.
Lokayukta police superintendents have been directed to examine relevant documents and materials, inspect the shoes supplied to students, conduct a preliminary investigation and submit a report within two weeks.
The order also noted possible violations concerning children’s right to education under Article 21A of the Constitution.

briefs.headline: Karnataka Public Service Commission scam: Tout paid Rs 11L for 23 air tickets of IAS officer, female friend
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: The 
CID
, probing the alleged job-for-cash scam involving the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), has told a court that accused Basavaraj Kannale allegedly paid around Rs 11 lakh for 23 air tickets and other expenses incurred by suspended IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar and a woman known to him.
The prosecution made the submission while opposing the bail pleas of Gangwar and Kannale. Special public prosecutor KL Bhagyalakshmi placed documents and other records before the court.
According to the prosecution, the air tickets were purchased through Bhagavati Enterprises in Bidar, a firm owned by Kannale.
The CID alleged that Gangwar and the woman travelled to several destinations this year, with Kannale allegedly bearing the expenses using money paid by civil service aspirants who were allegedly provided leaked question papers.
The CID alleged that Gangwar gifted gold and diamond jewellery worth around Rs 54 lakh to the woman in March and June.
Of this, Rs 2.9 lakh was allegedly paid in cash and through a credit card, while the remaining amount was transferred to Bhima Jewellers from bank accounts linked to Om Lakshmi Souhardha Sahakari Sangha Niyamita, a Bidar-based cooperative society.
The prosecution said the accounts were held by persons known to Kannale, who allegedly instructed KPSC candidates to transfer money to them.
The CID also produced panchanama copies relating to gold and diamond ornaments allegedly seized from Jaiswal, along with records of a resort booking in Devanahalli and other arrangements allegedly made for candidates who received the question paper and a ready answer script.
“CID has found that Kannale had asked KPSC candidates to make online transfers to those accounts,” Bhagyalakshmi said, adding that CCTV footage showed Gangwar and the woman purchasing jewellery at a showroom.
The prosecution claimed investigators had traced payments made by 11 aspiring candidates, totalling around Rs 60 lakh-Rs 70 lakh. The court is examining the material placed by the investigating agency while considering the bail applications.
ED arrests Gangwar, Kannale
The Enforcement Directorate has arrested suspended IAS officer Gangwar and his associate Kannale in connection with the scam.
The agency had sought body warrants to question them in prison. After collecting documents and alleging that the two were not cooperating, the ED arrested them Friday and took them for questioning Saturday.
What is Kannale’s role?
Investigators said Kannale’s financial fortunes rose after he met Gangwar in 2019, when Gangwar was CEO of Bidar. Kannale later expanded his business interests, allegedly gaining further opportunities when Gangwar served as KPSC Exam Controller from 2024 until March 2026.
Kannale, who identifies himself as a BJP worker, had earlier served as personal aide to former minister CN Ashwathnarayan.

briefs.headline: Karnataka BJP MLA raises Vande Mataram issue, triggers commotion
briefs.bodyText:
Shivamogga:
 BJP MLA SN Channabasappa has once again objected to the singing of only two stanzas of 
Vande Mataram
, this time raising the issue on stage in the presence of chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 at a govt programme in Thirthahalli.
Channabasappa had on Sept 16 walked out of a govt programme marking International Democracy Day in Shivamogga, where he was presiding over the function, after only two stanzas of Vande Mataram were sung.
Saturday, shortly after two stanzas of Vande Mataram were sung at an interaction on the Kasturirangan report on Western Ghats eco-sensitive zones, followed by the state song, the MLA took the microphone and appealed to Shivakumar to allow the full song to be sung.
“I’m standing here to make a request to the CM. He is doing a lot of good work, but as an attempt is made by the govt to hurt our sentiments, it has hurt us,” he said. “Your decision to have only two stanzas of Vande Mataram recited is having an impact on the people of the state. My only request is that the full Vande Mataram be recited. I have no other request. Please give an opportunity for the full Vande Mataram to be recited,” Channabasappa said.
His intervention triggered a brief commotion, with some people in the audience raising slogans and asking him to move away. A few people on the stage also surrounded him and urged him to return to his seat. Channabasappa then approached Shivakumar and spoke to him briefly, following which the CM was seen patting the MLA. Channabasappa later left the programme.
Reacting later, Shivakumar said the state govt would continue with the 
Congress
’ traditional position of singing only the first two stanzas at public and official programmes. He said Channabasappa had come to do politics rather than raise a concern and that he was not willing to engage in it. “The people’s response is an answer to the MLA,” Shivakumar added.

stories.headline: Life is a marathon, not a sprint, says Tata Sons’ Chandrasekaran
stories.bodyText:
Chennai:“Life is a marathon race, not a sprint. It is about becoming better by the day, not overtaking others. There will be ups and downs. Don’t fear downs, and do not turn your confidence into arrogance. Enjoy the journey,” 
Tata Sons
 chairman 
N Chandrasekaran
 said on Saturday.
Delivering his address at SAI University in Chengalpattu, he said: “It applies to both sports and life. It is all about the willingness to put in the effort to prepare, and not about winning. Understanding what it takes to win is crucial.”
Stating that he himself is a runner, a hobby he took up 18 years ago, he advised students to run for themselves with a clear target in mind.
Chandrasekaran said the world was full to the brim with possibilities, though it was rapidly changing, disruptive, and increasingly AI-led.
“It may be unnerving to read through the negative stories about job losses due to AI and so on. But a number of new sectors are opening. The art of the possible is becoming clear every day with AI and it is going to throw up so many things we have not imagined today. New industries will come up in the next five years, but we may not even know their terminology yet. 
And India is in a very strong position. India’s economic growth will be unparalleled in our own history and in any part of the world,” he said.
Chandrasekaran urged the young generation to keep learning and use social media to their benefit. “Make sure you read, watch and listen to what you choose to,” he said.
“To earn the right to feel the pressure is a privilege,” he said, quoting tennis legend Billie Jean King. Pressure would be a constant in one’s life after graduating from college and youngsters should learn to enjoy it all through their life, he said.

stories.headline: Tiruppur yarn producers seek support from garment units to modify role of CCI
stories.bodyText:
The Tirupur Yarn Manufacturers Association has called for support from the garment units in seeking steps by the Union government to change the role of the Cotton Corporation of India (CCI).
The China National Cotton Reserves Corporation maintains more than a year’s cotton stock and ensures stability in cotton prices. The CCI should, as such, not only procure cotton from the farmers at Minimum Support Price but also keep stocks and support the textile industry with stable raw material prices, the association said in a memorandum to the Apparel Export Promotion Council (AEPC) and the Tiruppur Exporters Association (TEA).
Office-bearers of the Tirupur Yarn Manufacturers Association met A. Sakthivel, chairman of the AEPC, and K.M. Subramanian, president of the TEA, on Saturday (September 19). They pointed out that many garment buyers and brands nominate specific ginners for cotton procurement, leaving spinning mills with limited access to credit.
The mills make upfront payments to buy cotton from the nominated ginners. However, many garment manufacturers continue to avail of credit from the mills for long durations. This has resulted in a significant working capital imbalance across the textile value chain, it said.
Yarn price is influenced by cotton price that accounts for 65%-70% of yarn manufacturing cost. The steep increase in cotton prices (around 30% in the domestic market and 50% in the international market) reflected in the yarn prices. With international cotton prices softening to 82.17 cents a pound from 91.55 cents a pound, yarn prices also declined to ₹379 a kg from ₹384 a kg.
Further, over 70% spinning mills could not modernise in the recent years as yarn exports were sluggish. Of the 45 million spindle working capacity in the country, over 20 million are more than 10 years old. If the mills do not modernise, there will be shortage of yarn, the yarn manufacturers reasoned.
In such a situation, the association sought the support of the garment sector for total removal of the 11% import duty on cotton and modifying the role of the CCI.
The garment industry should also ensure timely payments to the spinning mills within the mutually agreed credit terms. “We seek your cooperation in ensuring a more balanced payment mechanism across the value chain, particularly in view of the prevailing financial pressures on the spinning sector,” the yarn manufacturers association said.

stories.headline: Battle lines in the boardroom | Tata Sons
stories.deck: The group’s promoter company faces questions over leadership, ownership and regulatory issues amid growing differences over who should serve as its executive chairman and whether the company should be listed
stories.bodyText:
Tata Sons Pvt. Ltd., the principal investment holding company and promoter of Tata Group companies, was established in December 1917 as a trading firm to manage the profits of its operating businesses. Headquartered at Bombay House in South Mumbai, Tata Sons earns its income from dividends paid by its operating companies. It is governed by a board comprising executive chairman N. Chandrasekaran; Tata Trusts’ nominee directors Venu Srinivasan and Noel Naval Tata; independent directors Harish Manwani and Anita M. George; and executive director and chief financial officer (CFO) Saurabh Agarwal.
Today, Tata Sons, the group’s promoter company, faces questions over leadership, ownership and regularly issues amid growing differences over who should serve as its executive chairman and whether the company should be listed.
Tata Trusts, the philanthropic trusts established by contributions from members of the Tata family, own 66% of the equity capital of Tata Sons. Noel Naval Tata, as chairman, heads the Tata Trusts. Through dividend income from Tata Sons, the Tata Trusts support education, health, livelihood generation, scientific research and art and culture across the country.
Until 2017, the company was known as Tata Sons Ltd., a public company. It was made private that year and renamed Tata Sons Pvt. Ltd. Some of the large group companies in which Tata Sons has investments include Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Tata Steel, Tata Motors, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Tata Chemicals, Tata Elxsi, Titan, Trent, Tata Power, Tata Capital and Tata Consumer Products. It has several unlisted companies as well, including Tata Projects, Tata Advanced Systems, Tata Digital and Air India. In recent years, it has invested in new businesses such as semiconductors, electronics manufacturing, batteries, aviation, digital commerce, telecom equipment and defence manufacturing.
Each Tata company or enterprise operates independently under its own board of directors. An unusual business entity, Tata Sons is majority-owned by philanthropic trusts, manages independently run companies and is privately held. This distinctive structure has defined the Tata group for more than a century.
Tata Sons was established during the chairmanship of Sir Dorabji Tata, the elder son of Tata Group founder Jamsetji Tata, who served as chairman from 1904 to 1932. The other chairmen of Tata Sons included Sir Nowroji Saklatvala, J.R.D. Tata, Ratan Naval Tata, Cyrus Mistry and, currently, Natarajan Chandrasekaran.
Besides Tata Trusts, the other shareholders of Tata Sons include the Shapoorji Pallonji Group (SP Group), with an 18% holding; Tata Group companies, with about 13%; and individuals, mostly Tata family members, who hold about 3%. For FY2026, Tata Sons reported a standalone profit of ₹31,961 crore, up 22% from the previous year, while revenue increased 9.1% to ₹42,367 crore. Consolidated revenue reached ₹16.24 lakh crore, and profit rose 52% to ₹1.71 lakh crore.
Multiple challenges
While Tata Trusts, the majority shareholders, have opposed and disputed the September 17 re-appointment of executive chairman for a third term starting in February 2027, the company’s board has ratified the decision. The move has brought the board into confrontation with the majority stakeholder, led by Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata, raising questions over who ultimately governs Tata Sons.
There was another development that heightened the tensions within the group. In a major regulatory development, the Reserve Bank of India, on September 11, 2026, rejected Tata Sons’ application, made on March 28, 2024, for voluntary surrender of its Certificate of Registration to be classified as an unregistered Core Investment Company (CIC).
The RBI, after keeping the application under examination for nearly two and a half years, directed Tata Sons to comply with the regulations applicable to upper-layer non-banking finance companies (NBFCs), a move that has been interpreted as mandatory stock exchange listing. Under RBI rules, NBFCs in the upper layer are subject to enhanced requirements, including mandatory listing within the prescribed regulatory framework.
While the company’s board, by a majority vote, has approved a resolution to comply with the RBI’s directive, its majority owner, Tata Trusts, does not want the company to be listed. The Trusts argue that keeping Tata Sons privately held is integral to the ownership model through which dividends support philanthropy.
With these two major developments, the conflict between the Tata Sons board and Tata Trusts has become public. Both sides are preparing for a bitter legal battle, which could be a replay of what happened a decade ago.
Ten years ago, the Tata Trusts had to assert their authority to oust then Tata Sons executive chairman, Cyrus Mistry, in a boardroom battle. In October 2016, Ratan Tata, who had retired as Tata Sons chairman in 2012, returned as its interim chairman and fought a bitter battle with Cyrus Mistry and the Shapoorji Pallonji Group (SP Group).
Mr. Chandrasekaran, then TCS managing director and chief executive, was appointed executive chairman of Tata Sons in February 2017.
Until his death in October 2024, Ratan Tata retained considerable influence over the affairs of Tata Sons. Ratan Tata first became chairman of Tata Sons in 1991 and continued until 2012. He also headed Tata Trusts, leaving little scope for a conflict between the company and its shareholders.
Increasing differences
Differences have surfaced since Noel Tata, the half-brother of Ratan Tata, took over as Tata Trusts chairman in October 2024. Over the past few months, the differences have become increasingly visible. The matter has been complicated further by the SP Group’s support for a listing, as it seeks to monetise its stake to meet its financial obligations.
The Tata Trusts have offered the SP Group an opportunity to dilute its stake, valued at about ₹25,000 crore, in 18 months to avoid a listing. But in a recent statement, SP Group chairman Shapoorji Pallonji Mistry, who is Noel Tata’s brother-in-law, welcomed the RBI’s decision and backed the listing of Tata Sons.
Tata Sons is today a combination of an investment holding company, a capital allocator, a promoter of dozens of businesses and a bridge between a large commercial conglomerate and its philanthropic owners. As battle lines are drawn between the Tata Sons board and its majority shareholder, the coming months will determine whether the board or its majority owner prevails. More fundamentally, the tussle raises a question about the future of Tata’s distinctive ownership model and whether it can survive in its present form.

stories.deck: Consumers who have not undergone BAA will not be stopped from receiving LPG cylinders. However, those who choose not to complete the authentication will have to pay the prevailing market price and will not receive the subsidy.
stories.bodyText:
LPG refill Aadhaar authentication rule: Domestic LPG consumers who have not yet completed their Biometric Aadhaar Authentication (BAA) will have to complete the process to book subsidised cylinder refills at regulated prices from October 1, 2026.
The Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry has said no further action will be required from the 27.43 crore consumers who have already completed the Aadhaar authentication.
As of September 19, biometric authentication had been completed by 89.9% of active domestic LPG consumers.
What happens if you don’t complete Aadhaar authentication for LPG
Consumers who have not undergone BAA will not be stopped from receiving LPG cylinders. However, those who choose not to complete the authentication will have to pay the prevailing market price and will not receive the subsidy.
According to the government, the authentication requirement is intended to ensure that subsidised LPG benefits reach eligible households and to curb the diversion of domestic LPG cylinders for commercial and industrial use.
How consumers can complete authentication
Consumers have several options to complete Biometric Aadhaar Authentication. They can do it at the time of cylinder delivery, visit their LPG distributor's showroom, or use the mobile application provided by their oil marketing company.
Indane customers can complete the process through IndianOil ONE, while Bharatgas customers can use HelloBPCL. HP Gas consumers can authenticate through the HP PAY app.
Consumers who do not want to complete the authentication will have to record their choice through the digital channels of their respective oil marketing companies. They can still receive cylinders, but these will be supplied at market prices and will depend on local availability, according to an ET report.
Subsidy and compensation
Domestic LPG is sold at a price below its cost. The implicit subsidy on a 14.2-kg cylinder is estimated at around Rs 210 for September 2026, down from Rs 721 in June.
The government said it provided Rs 22,000 crore in compensation to oil marketing companies in FY23. It is paying Rs 30,000 crore in compensation in FY26 and FY27. As of August 31, 2026, the companies' accumulated under-recoveries from domestic LPG had crossed Rs 62,000 crore.
Consumers seeking help with LPG-related services can contact the toll-free helpline at 1800 2333 555.
PNG push
Meanwhile, despite the government's push to encourage a shift to cleaner piped gas, only around 20% of LPG consumers who have a PNG network in their neighbourhood and are eligible to make the switch have actually converted to PNG. The push followed the military conflict in West Asia earlier this year.
According to government data, city gas distribution (CGD) companies had identified 21.7 lakh consumers who had access to a PNG network and were eligible to switch. Of these, only 4.4 lakh consumers have applied so far, while PNG connections have been activated for 3.3 lakh consumers.
The identified consumers are located across more than 72,000 housing societies in 311 geographical areas. These areas have PNG networks operated by oil companies as well as public sector and private CGD entities.
Government data showed that more than 21 lakh households were contacted through WhatsApp messages, while eight lakh households received physical notices urging them to shift to PNG. More than 33,000 camps were also conducted as part of the exercise. Despite these efforts, the conversion rate remained low. Over the past five months, just over 1.4 lakh households have surrendered their LPG connections.
The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board had earlier launched two campaigns to encourage the adoption of PNG. However, the government's efforts intensified during the peak of the West Asia conflict in March and April, when disruptions to supplies through the Strait of Hormuz put pressure on India's LPG imports.
India consumed 33 million tonnes of LPG in 2025-26. Domestic production accounted for about 13 MT, while imports met the remaining requirement, with most of these supplies coming from West Asia. In contrast, the country is relatively more comfortable in terms of LNG supplies and domestic gas production.

briefs.headline: How sanctioned ships are heading to Alang for recycling
briefs.bodyText:
During its blockade of Venezuela in December of last year, the U.S. government sought to seize several tankers that were calling on Venezuela. Among them were Marinera, which the U.S. pursued for nearly a month and seized off Iceland, and Lileo. In August, the U.S. government sold the two vessels to GMS, a leading buyer of vessels going for demolition, which has brought them to Alang in Gujarat for recycling.
Marinera and Lileo are among the more than thousand vessels sanctioned by the U.S. While these two were directly sold by the U.S. government, many sanctioned ships owned by sanctioned entities have been coming to Alang for recycling in recent months. For instance, Lloyd’s List reported on Sept. 4 that the Double In, a Very Large Gas Carrier that had been sanctioned by the U.S. for dealing in Iranian cargoes, had beached in Alang for recycling after ownership was transferred to a shell company.
It would seem that beyond just the age of the vessel, the renewed focus on such ships due to the West Asia crisis has made operating some of these ships more challenging. For instance, eight sanctioned ships Lloyds List had identified as having scrapped in January and February this year, four were built well into the 2000s, which means they were not quite old enough for demolition. Blockades, interdiction of these vessels in the seas, and choking of demand are contributing to this trend, say industry sources.
“Bangladesh, which is the leading ship recycling nation in the world, as well as Pakistan, are not accepting sanctioned ships for recycling, so India is becoming the major destination for sanctioned vessel recycling,” says Anil Sharma, founder and CEO of GMS. Companies such as GMS purchase the vessel, prepare it for recycling, and bring it to the recycling yard to which they have sold the vessel.
Sanctions by the U.S. will lock the ship owner and related firms out of the mainstream global financial system. Indian banks and financial firms will therefore not accept transactions involving these entities. Industry sources say that there is typically an Indian firm in the chain so the immediate transactions of recycling are conducted in rupees but eventually the money could be routed through other channels such as the Hong Kong dollar, digital-crypto currencies, and rupee-rouble exchanges to the firms sanctioned by the U.S.
But the U.S. and other sanctioning entities are not entirely averse to scrapping of the ships they have sanctioned. They see it as a route to put the ships out of business. A U.S. treasury department official, for instance, wrote in an email to The Hindu: “To protect maritime safety, we are committed to responsible solutions to get sanctioned vessels off the water. We consider these matters on a case-by-case basis.” The European Union is considering such case-by-case approvals of demolitions of ships dealing with Russian oil it has sanctioned.
The U.S. government has put together a process for approving such demolitions for recycling. “The U.S. government may approve such demolitions if the money was not going towards funding what the U.S. government had a problem with in the first place. For instance, it may approve if the money was going to repay a loan taken from a non-sanctioned bank before the sanctions or if it would go to paying unpaid crew wages and so on,” adds Mr. Sharma.
GMS has acquired six approvals from the U.S. government. The first approval took seven months while the following ones were quicker.
Indian regulations
India’s Recycling of Ships Regulations 2026 primarily updates the regulations on compliance with recent international rules such as the Hong Kong Convention. It does not specifically address the issue of ships sanctioned by the U.S. and EU. Officially, the Indian government does not recognize these sanctions and recognizes only those by the United Nations. Nevertheless, the regulations do talk about scrutinizing the documents submitted by the ship owner by the Director General of Maritime Affairs for authenticity to clamp down on fraud.
For Alang, the competent authority to handle the ships is the Gujarat Maritime Board. The 2026 regulations specify that the ship recycler shall submit to the authority the originals of: Certificate of Registry; valid third-party/oil-pollution insurance certificate; certificates of competency for master/officers/ratings; Inventory of Hazardous Materials (IHM) certificate and/or Ready for Recycling Certificate among other documents.
If any of the documents submitted is found to be unreliable, or if a submitted document is found to be fake or conceals a material fact, the shipowner shall not be given permission to anchor, enter, beach, or begin cutting, as per the regulations. Sanctioned ships often sail without proper insurance such as P&I or the IHM certificate. And India’s regulations specifically talk about insurance covering “third-party liability, oil pollution damage, and wreck removal” and the IHM certificate
